top_findings.title: Not an actual MCP-protocol server despite the name
top_findings.evidence: soccer_mcp/server.py:10-113 — SoccerMCPServer is a plain in-process Python class. Grep across the tree for MCP SDK usage (import mcp / from mcp / fastmcp / mcp.server / stdio_server / list_tools / call_tool / types.Tool) returns NONE; the only 'mcp' tokens are the local package name soccer_mcp and the class name. Dispatch is a local handlers dict (server.py:40-76) behind execute_query(name, **kwargs) (server.py:78-113). No server entrypoint, no stdio/transport, no tool schemas — soccer_mcp/__init__.py exposes only the class; the sole __main__ is in tests/test_soccer_mcp.py:334.
top_findings.suggestion: Wrap the existing handlers dict in an MCP SDK server (e.g. `from mcp.server import Server` or fastmcp), register each query as a tool with an input schema, and add a stdio entrypoint (python -m soccer_mcp). The query layer is already complete; only the protocol shell is missing.
